correctness.rationale: A binary-increment recurrence yields an exact bounded martingale decomposition, with predictable variance \(pq\) times the preceding binary state. Its strong law and martingale functional CLT fix the variance \(pq/(1+q)^3\). The last adjacent-parent success is a common ancestor of all later vertices, yielding a deterministic uniform pairwise-distance error bounded by twice one plus the longest failure run. The latter is \(O(\log n)\) almost surely. These facts give a \(C([0,1]^2)\) Brownian-increment field, uniform line-segment metric-measure limit, diameter CLT, and integrated-Brownian mean pair distance variance \(2\sigma^2/15\). The complete checker passes 708747 finite assertions; it is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The exact Bernoulli recursive-tree source studies one-ended topology and infinite collisions; quantitative all-pair graph geometry, the covariance of shared birth-interval fluctuations, and the sharp variance of mean pair distances provide a natural missing statistical layer of this model. Unlike a single Markov chain height CLT, this establishes a global metric space limit and a Gaussian field controlling every pair simultaneously, allowing nontrivial diameter and Wiener-index projections. The result is structurally motivated and not a finite-table recitation.
